chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: After importing the NumPy library, we are all set to fit a line to our scatter plot.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: So we have a set of points and we want a line which has an equation of degree one.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: So we go ahead and fit a polynomial of degree one.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: This is what polyfit function of the NumPy does.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: So let's use it.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: We will first do it for SPY and XORM.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: For us, the x coordinates are the daily return values for SPY and

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: the y coordinates are daily return values for the XORM.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: The one denotes the degree of our function.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Calling this function will return two things.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: The first is the polynomial coefficient and the second is the intercept.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Since we have a polynomial of degree one, it would be of the form y is equal to mx plus b.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: So m is the coefficient and b is the intercept.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: We named them as beta and alpha, just as Professor explained.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Now we finally plot these values.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: The idea for plotting the line is, for every value of x, that is SPY,

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: we find a value of y using the line equation, which is mx plus b.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: This parameter denotes that we want a line plot with a color red.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Now let's check our graph.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Here is the fitted line.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Now let's do it for gold, so that we can compare them both.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: We also print the beta and the alpha values for each.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Now let's compare the beta values, which shows how the stock moves with respect to SPY.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: You can see that the beta values for the x-om is greater as compared to that of gold,

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: which means that x-om is more reactive to market as compared to gold.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: On the other hand, the alpha values denote how well it performed with respect to SPY.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Numbers over here say that gold performed better.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Let's cross check.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: You can see the upward movement of the gold as compared to the SPY.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: One last thing is to find the correlation.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Yet again, the data frame has a function CORR, which means correlation.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: And we can define which method to use.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: We use the method Pearson.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: It is the most commonly used method to calculate the correlation.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: There are other methods as well.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Check the instructor's note for more detail.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: We get the output in the matrix format with correlation of each column with each other column.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: You can see that the SPY and the x-om are highly correlated.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: The value of the correlation for gold and SPY is very small.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: Let's check the graph.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: You can observe that the dots do not fit the line closely.

chunks.title: Scatterplots in python_1
chunks.text: And that's why the correlation value for the SPY versus gold is less as compared to SPY versus exome.
